All three lineages, retrieved in the same release, run root → class d (Alpha and beta proteins, a+b, sunid 53931) → fold d.15 (beta-Grasp, ubiquitin-like, sunid 54235; fold annotation: core beta(2)-alpha-beta(2), mixed beta-sheet 2143) → superfamily d.15.1 (Ubiquitin-like, sunid 54236). Family-level Pfam cross-references confirm the families are curated as distinct sequence groups: d.15.1.1 → PF00240; d.15.1.2 → PF00789; d.15.1.5 → PF00788 and PF02196. Family members retrieved: d.15.1.1 contains ubiquitin itself, SUMO-1/2/3, Nedd8, Rub1, Elongin B, hub1, Ubl3/Ubl5/Ubl7, ISG15 (interferon-induced 15 kDa protein), and ubiquitin-like domains of parkin, Rad23 (Hhr23a/B), PLIC-2, tubulin folding cofactor B, etc.; d.15.1.2 contains Faf1, p47, KIAA0794, TUG, UBXD6/Reproduction 8; d.15.1.5 contains c-Raf1 RBD, A-Raf, RalGDS, Rlf, Rgl, RapGEF5, byr2, PI3K, PLC-epsilon-1, afadin, GRB-7, RGS14, RASSF8, plus 'automated matches' proteins in each family. Homology records for the superfamily (scope sf) and for all three families (scope fa) return homology_implied_by_level=true with no warnings or heterogeneity flags; representative domains d1h8ca_ (Faf1 UBX, d.15.1.2) and d2c5ld_ (RBD, automated match to d2byfa1, complexed with GTP/Mg, d.15.1.5) also carry no homology warnings. The superfamily d.15.1 has no comments or inconsistencies recorded.

**Biologically useful relationship SCOPe supports.** The deepest shared homology-bearing node is the superfamily d.15.1. SCOPe therefore asserts probable common evolutionary ancestry among ubiquitin-related proteins, UBX domains, and Ras-binding domains: they are divergent descendants of one ubiquitin-like (beta-grasp) ancestor that share conserved core architecture, not merely a convergent fold. Because they are placed in different families, SCOPe does not assert the closer, sequence-detectable relationship that holds within a family (e.g., ubiquitin to SUMO or Nedd8 inside d.15.1.1). This is the useful inference: a UBX domain or an RBD can be modelled and understood as a ubiquitin-like structural module, the fold's beta-grasp core and secondary-structure topology can be expected to be conserved, and remote-homology searches or structure superposition across the three families are evolutionarily justified. The fold level (d.15) is weaker still: fourteen other superfamilies share the beta-grasp fold (e.g., d.15.2 CAD & PB1, d.15.3 MoaD/ThiS, d.15.4 2Fe-2S ferredoxin-like, d.15.7 immunoglobulin-binding domains, d.15.15 PI3K ABD-like); for those SCOPe asserts only structural similarity, makes no positive homology claim, and that absence must not be strengthened to 'unrelated' or 'convergent'.

**Annotation transfer that would be unsafe.** Superfamily co-membership supports ancestry, not function, so the following transfers are not supported by SCOPe: (1) Transferring ubiquitin-family function to UBX or RBD domains—UBX domains (Faf1, p47, TUG) and RBDs are not post-translational modifiers; they are not conjugated to substrates, lack the C-terminal Gly-Gly activation/ligation chemistry, and do not imply E1/E2/E3 processing, proteasomal targeting, or deubiquitinase susceptibility. (2) Transferring RBD function (GTP-bound Ras/Rap/Ral effector binding, as seen with c-Raf1, RalGDS, PI3K, PLC-epsilon) to ubiquitin, SUMO, Nedd8, or UBX domains—the Ras-binding surface and partner specificity are family-level properties not implied by d.15.1 placement. (3) Transferring UBX function (p97/VCP/Cdc48 cofactor binding) to ubiquitin-related or RBD members. (4) Assuming interchangeable binding partners, interaction surfaces, substrate specificity, pathway roles, oligomeric state, or ligand binding (the GTP/Mg annotation on d2c5ld_ describes the complex in that PDB entry and does not transfer to other families or even other RBD entries). (6) Treating cross-family members as interchangeable structural templates for atomic-detail modelling of loops, binding surfaces, or interface residues; the beta-grasp core is a reasonable template only at the topology/core level. (7) Treating the 'automated matches' proteins as curator-reviewed assertions of function; they are automated assignments and the Pfam cross-references apply to the curated families, not to automated members per se.
